problems.quote: roughly three quarters of an English word
problems.issue: Used as the definition of a token. That is only a rough English-prose average; code, JSON, and non-Latin text are often far denser, so budgets set from this will be wrong.
problems.fix: Call it an English-prose ranking heuristic and require a provider tokenizer before any hard budget.

problems.quote: One timestamp at the top of a prompt can zero your cache hit rate
problems.issue: Overstated. Automatic prefix caching is provider-specific, often has a minimum length and TTL, and some APIs cache only at explicit breakpoints. A leading timestamp does not always zero the discount, and a cache write can cost more than a miss.
problems.fix: Say it can invalidate an implicit prefix cache when that feature applies, and model cache-write fees separately.

problems.issue: Treats always-loaded tokens as full-price input on every session. If the prefix is cached, marginal cost is much lower; if sessions do not actually load hot.md, the 255-token total is inflated.
problems.fix: Label it uncached worst case and multiply cached vs fresh shares by the user's price table.

problems.issue: Does not follow from re-sending prior turns: 700*(60*61/2)=1,281,000. Three sessions of 20 are about 441,000, not 244,300, so the '82% fewer' worked example is not reproducible from the stated inputs.
problems.fix: Publish the exact formula or replace the numbers with ones the formula produces.

problems.quote: A planted lie passes a model reviewer more often than you would think
problems.issue: The receipt only shows a non-verbatim quote fails a string check. A false sentence copied from a bad source passes; a true paraphrase fails. No evidence is given that models wave the planted line through.
problems.fix: Claim only 'verbatim quote mismatch is caught'; state cherry-picked and paraphrased claims are not.

problems.quote: A model does not get bored, does not forget a cross-reference
problems.issue: False. Models drop links, invent pages, and skip contradictions, which is why the linter exists. This encourages unattended multi-file edits.
problems.fix: Say a model can attempt the upkeep; the manifest, diff, and lint are what keep it honest.

problems.issue: The guard avoids a model call only if it runs before the agent. status still walks the vault; a cron that starts the agent first still pays. 'Prints nothing' also disagrees with chapter 14's 'empty list'.
problems.fix: Claim 'no model call if the shell guard sees no pending files' and note status CPU cost.

problems.quote: Compacting a log removes most of its characters without losing the failure
problems.issue: Head/tail compaction drops failures that sit in the middle. The sample keeps the error only because it is in the tail.
problems.fix: Always keep lines matching error/fail/exception, then head/tail the rest.

problems.quote: The checks in this repo spend zero tokens
problems.issue: The tools do, but the recommended post-edit hook sends lint text back into the model, and chapter 4.6 adds HEAD requests. The grep receipt misses urllib. Link-rot on wiki URLs is an SSRF risk.
problems.fix: Limit the claim to tools/*.py model calls; warn that hooks spend tokens and URL fetches need an allow-list.

problems.quote: Below roughly 50 to 100 sources a wiki is not worth building
problems.issue: Presented as a crossover with retrieval, with no measurement. Index fit, query repetition, and synthesis cost dominate, not source count.
problems.fix: Replace with a measured test: if the same facts are re-explained often and the index fits, build it; otherwise search.

keep: Measure usage and always-loaded size before changing prompts.
Content-hash manifests so unchanged sources never trigger ingest.
Deterministic quote, link, and budget checks instead of model self-review.
Stable prefix first, volatile text last, when the provider actually prefix-caches.
Cheap-first routing that yields to an explicit quality or model request.

techniques.name: reasoning-effort gate
techniques.saves: Thinking tokens often dwarf visible output; skipping extended reasoning on easy calls is a large cut.
techniques.risk: Hard multi-step and math tasks get shallow, wrong answers.

tool.algorithm: Input: task text plus a flag if tools or citations are required. Score length, digit density, and markers like prove/compare/debug. Output JSON {effort: none|low|high}. Default none unless score>=2 or the user named quality.

techniques.name: extractive query prune
techniques.saves: Sends a few overlapping windows instead of a whole file, cutting input on doc QA.
techniques.risk: Answer lives outside the lexical window; names and paraphrases are missed.

tool.algorithm: Input: query and a text file. Split on blank lines, score windows by shared lowercase tokens, take top 3 with one neighbour. Output those slices plus byte offsets. No model.

techniques.name: history tool-result strip
techniques.saves: Repeated tool dumps dominate multi-turn input; keep the last result and a one-line status for older ones.
techniques.risk: A later turn needed an earlier full payload.

tool.algorithm: Input: JSONL turns. For each tool-result role, if an identical tool id appears later, replace body with '[prior result omitted, N chars]'. Output JSONL and chars saved. Never touch the last user turn.

techniques.name: near-duplicate query cache
techniques.saves: Exact caches miss rephrasings; a shingle hit avoids a second generation.
techniques.risk: Similar wording, different entity or date, returns the wrong stored answer.

tool.algorithm: Input: query plus optional store. 5-shingle Jaccard against cached keys. If max>=0.9 and model/prompt version match, print the stored answer; else exit 1. Store with sha256 of model+version+query.

techniques.name: markdown diet
techniques.saves: Badges, HTML comments, and base64 images are huge and rarely affect the answer.
techniques.risk: The question was about a figure or a commented-out spec.

tool.algorithm: Input: markdown path. Drop HTML comments, badge image links, and data: URIs; collapse blank lines. Output diet.md plus a JSON report of bytes removed by class. Do not touch fenced code.

techniques.name: prefix canonicalizer
techniques.saves: Unstable key order and tool order shatter prefix caches across calls that are otherwise identical.
techniques.risk: A downstream parser depended on original order.

tool.algorithm: Input: JSON request. Sort object keys, sort tool definitions by name, move a date/id field to a trailing 'volatile' object. Output canonical JSON and a hash of the stable prefix only.

techniques.name: retry preflight
techniques.saves: Schema and length failures cause full-price retries; catch them before the call.
techniques.risk: Over-strict local rules reject outputs the API would have accepted.

tool.algorithm: Input: draft output, max tokens, required keys. Reject if estimated tokens exceed max, JSON does not parse, or required keys are missing. Output {ok, reason}. Exit 2 on fail so a script can fix without a model.

techniques.name: flex-tier picker
techniques.saves: Latency-tolerant jobs can use flex/batch discounts beyond a single batch flag.
techniques.risk: Using flex for a waiting user, or a tier that drops quality/SLA.

tool.algorithm: Input: prices JSON, deadline seconds, interactive bool. If interactive or deadline<60, pick standard; elif deadline>3600 pick batch; else flex. Output route name and estimated USD. Never call a network.

workflows.name: cascade with accept gate
steps: Call the smallest model with think_gate effort none.
Accept only if qcache miss was real and a deterministic check passes.
Else one higher rung, never skipping the user's named model.

workflows.name: doc QA without the whole file
steps: Answer from slices only; if the model says not-in-context, widen once.
Store the accepted answer in qcache.py.

workflows.name: long agent thread diet
steps: canon.py the stable system and tool block.
session_budget.py only after strip, so the split decision is not based on duplicate tool dumps.

workflows.name: overnight price lane
steps: Reject the job if a human is waiting.
canon.py so the batch shares one prefix.
Validate with preflight.py; requeue failures only.
